story: Court supply is not evenly spread. Hertsmere sits at 26 courts per 100,000 people, while the GB average is 4.5 and 38 councils with more than 100,000 residents still have none.
hold_back: Use Padel Genie catchment analysis to filter any catchment for warehouses, sports clubs, schools, car parks and brownfield land.
why_it_works: It gives one sharp local ranking with named councils, then widens the point with the zero-court count so the post feels useful rather than abstract.
improve: It would be better with a verified product atom confirming a saved view or list for the 38 councils with none, rather than only the catchment filters.

story: Carbon Padel Club in Manchester has 17 courts. The average UK club has 3.4 and the median is 3, so the biggest sites are still outliers rather than the norm.
hold_back: Check the free map for club footprints, then use paid catchment analysis and planning details to assess where large-format sites may fit.

improve: It would improve with a verified atom for a named Club X-Ray or club detail page so the hold-back could point to a specific product view, not just general analysis.

story: Supply per head is uneven across the UK. Northern Ireland leads at 6.52 courts per 100,000 people, while Scotland is on 2.06 and London on 3.8.
hold_back: Use the free map for every open court and a free preview of the planning pipeline and catchment analysis across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

improve: It would be better with a verified atom for a saved regional view or named catchment example inside the product, so the hold-back could be more specific than the general preview.

story: Sheffield is not waiting around. It already has 51 open courts and also approved 10 new schemes in the last year, while East Riding of Yorkshire led approvals with 12.
hold_back: Use the free map for every open court, then the planning-pipeline preview and paid planning details to inspect local schemes and catchments.
